text.title: 账本旁的两根柱子
text.situation:
杰伊在账本旁的纸上画了两根柱子。它们表示四月销售数字：包带来 1800 英镑，维修带来 600 英镑。维修占总额四分之一。米娜核对数字后，杰伊才涂色。生意规模仍小，两根柱子也看不出工作是否轻松。在一张散页上，杰伊比较修伊莱提手和换一个完整包的价格。一处小接缝维修可能只花3英镑，只是18英镑新包价格的一小部分，但伊莱那次较大的维修几乎与新包一样贵。他把两个例子都写下来。米娜让图表留在楼上，顾客需要的是实际报价，不是基于平均值的承诺。

杰伊：维修占销售总额的百分之二十五。
米娜：对。两根柱子代表什么？
杰伊：卖包和维修的收入，尚未扣成本。
米娜：那图表就与销售账本放在一起，它不能替代某次维修的报价。

paragraphs.en: Jay drew two bars on paper beside the ledger. They represented the April sales figures: £1,800 from bags and £600 from repairs. Repairs accounted for a quarter of the total. Mina checked the numbers before Jay coloured the bars. The scale of the business was still small, and neither bar told them whether the work had been easy. On a loose sheet, Jay compared the price of repairing Eli’s handle with replacing a whole bag. A small seam repair might cost £3, only a fraction of the £18 price of a new bag, though Eli’s larger repair had cost nearly as much. He wrote both examples down. Mina left the chart upstairs rather than putting it in the window; customers needed the actual repair estimate, not a promise based on an average.

paragraphs.en:
Jay: Repairs account for twenty-five per cent of the sales total.
Mina: Yes. What do the two bars represent?
Jay: Money from bags and repairs, before costs.
Mina: Then keep the chart with the sales ledger. It cannot replace an estimate for a particular repair.

S08.Q18.P01.cue: 说明图表代表什么，以及维修所占的比例。
acceptableAnswers: 维修占销售总额四分之一。 两根柱子表示四月销售数字。

S08.Q18.P03.cue: 比较小接缝维修与新包的费用。
acceptableAnswers: 一处小接缝维修可能只花3英镑，只是18英镑新包价格的一小部分。

S08.Q18.T01.cue: 一种服务占总使用量百分之四十，怎么说明？
acceptableAnswers: 这项服务占总使用量百分之四十。
